proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Administration review the effectiveness of SBA loan and grant programs and report to Congress within six months, ranking programs by cost-effectiveness. It says the roughly 1 billion dollar agency budget should be held constant until Congress considers the report, after which ineffective programs would be ended, duplicative functions consolidated and money shifted to more effective programs or the budget reduced.

status_summary: No SBA review ranking its programs by cost-effectiveness and reported to Congress was found. The Administration's FY2026 request proposed about 0.8 billion dollars for SBA, but the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75, approved 2026-02-03) provided about 1.3 billion dollars, including 330 million for entrepreneurial development, according to CRS. CRS reported on 2026-05-27 that the FY2027 request seeks 329.0 million dollars, a 74.7 percent cut, funds entrepreneurial development only for veterans outreach (21.4 million dollars), and raises the Office of Advocacy to 14.1 million dollars; the Administration describes the cut programs as failed counseling and training programs but no ranking or evaluation is cited.

timeline.event: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 7148, Public Law 119-75) was approved, providing about 1.3 billion dollars for SBA per CRS, above the Administration's request of about 0.8 billion dollars.
CRS summarized the FY2027 SBA budget request of 329.0 million dollars, a 74.7 percent decrease from FY2026, which would end funding for most entrepreneurial development programs.

title: Rank SBA programs by cost-effectiveness, hold the budget flat, then end weak programs
uncertainties: One web search for an SBA program effectiveness review or report to Congress found only congressional letters and commentary, none read; absence of a report is an absence-of-evidence finding. The FY2026 request and enacted SBA amounts come from CRS; the appropriations law was confirmed on GovInfo by number and date only. The FY2027 request's own release date was not confirmed, so the event is dated by the CRS summary. FY2027 appropriations status was not checked. The budget requests propose ending programs without the ranking report the chapter asks for first, and they cut rather than hold the budget constant, so the match is parallel.
